title: IRDAI's Distribution Reset: Who Loses Margin, Who Keeps the Moat

beats.say: On the twenty third of September, IRDAI proposed the biggest change to how insurance is sold in India since commission caps were removed in twenty twenty three. Hard caps on commissions. Lower expense limits. And no more forcing insurance on borrowers.
beats.cap: On 23 September, IRDAI proposed the biggest change to how insurance is sold in India since commission caps were removed in 2023. Hard caps on commissions. Lower expense limits. And no more forcing insurance on borrowers.
cues: On 23 September, IRDAI proposed the biggest change to how insurance is sold
in India since commission caps were removed in 2023.
Hard caps on commissions.
Lower expense limits.
And no more forcing insurance on borrowers.

beats.say: Its own data explains why: payments to distributors have been growing four to five times faster than premiums. If the proposals stand, margin moves from distributors to policyholders, and the moat moves to insurers that already sell cheaply.
beats.cap: Its own data explains why: payments to distributors have been growing four to five times faster than premiums. If the proposals stand, margin moves from distributors to policyholders, and the moat moves to insurers that already sell cheaply.
cues: Its own data explains why:
payments to distributors have been growing four to five times faster than
premiums.
If the proposals stand, margin moves from distributors to policyholders,
and the moat moves to insurers that already sell cheaply.

beats.say: Chapter one. What went wrong.
beats.cap: Chapter one. What went wrong.
cues: Chapter one.
What went wrong.

beats.say: Private life insurers' total expenses fell from twenty one point three percent of premium in twenty fifteen to sixteen point five percent in twenty twenty one, then rose back to twenty point two percent last year. Private general insurers reached thirty two point one percent.
beats.cap: Private life insurers' total expenses fell from 21.3% of premium in FY15 to 16.5% in FY21, then rose back to 20.2% in FY26. Private general insurers reached 32.1% in FY26.

scene.heading: PRIVATE INSURERS' TOTAL EXPENSES, % OF PREMIUM

cues: Private life insurers' total expenses fell from 21.3% of premium in FY15 to
16.5% in FY21, then rose back to 20.2% in FY26.
Private general insurers reached 32.1% in FY26.

beats.say: In IRDAI's own words: the discipline achieved over a decade has been unwound in the space of a few years, and it is policyholders who have funded the reversal.
beats.cap: In IRDAI's own words: "The discipline achieved over a decade has been unwound in the space of a few years and it is policyholders who have funded the reversal."
cues: In IRDAI's own words:
"The discipline achieved over a decade has been unwound in the space of a few
years and it is policyholders who have funded the reversal."

beats.say: In the life corporate agency channel, new business premium grew twenty eight percent in two years, while distributor pay grew one hundred and twenty five percent. It is now nearly twenty seven percent of first year premium.
beats.cap: In the life corporate agency channel, new business premium grew 28% from FY23 to FY25, while distributor remuneration grew 125%. It is now "nearly 27% of first-year premium".
cues: In the life corporate agency channel,
new business premium grew 28% from FY23 to FY25,
while distributor remuneration grew 125%.
It is now "nearly 27% of first-year premium".

beats.say: Broker commissions in general insurance rose one hundred and seventy three percent, against thirty seven percent premium growth. And in credit linked insurance sold with loans, payouts average around forty two percent.
beats.cap: Broker commissions in general insurance rose 173%, against 37% premium growth. And in the NBFC channel, where 93% of business is credit life sold with loans, payouts average around 42%.
cues: Broker commissions in general insurance rose 173%, against 37% premium growth.
And in the NBFC channel, where 93% of business is credit life sold with
loans, payouts average around 42%.

beats.say: Chapter two. What IRDAI proposes.
beats.cap: Chapter two. What IRDAI proposes.
cues: Chapter two.
What IRDAI proposes.

beats.say: First, lower expense limits. Life insurers must reach fifteen percent of premium in two years, and twelve and a half percent in five. General insurers, twenty five percent and then twenty. Twenty twenty seven twenty eight is year one.
beats.cap: First, lower expense limits. Life insurers must reach 15% of premium in two years, and 12.5% in five. General insurers, 25% and then 20%. FY2027-28 is Year 1.
cues: First, lower expense limits.
Life insurers must reach 15% of premium in two years, and 12.5% in five.
General insurers, 25% and then 20%.
FY2027-28 is Year 1.

beats.say: Miss the path, and IRDAI can restrict new product launches, dividends, and in extreme cases new business through the channel responsible.
beats.cap: Miss the path, and IRDAI can impose "restrictions on new product launches, restrictions on dividend distribution", and in extreme cases on new business through the channel responsible.
cues: Miss the path, and IRDAI can impose "restrictions on new product launches,
restrictions on dividend distribution",
and in extreme cases on new business through the channel responsible.

beats.say: Second, hard commission caps. For individual health insurance, distributors such as brokers and banks can earn fifteen percent on a first sale, and only five percent on renewals. Agents get twenty and ten. On single premium savings policies, distributors get one percent.
beats.cap: Second, hard commission caps. For individual health insurance, distributors such as brokers and banks can earn 15% on a first sale, and only 5% on renewals. Agents get 20% and 10%. On single-premium savings policies, distributors get 1%.
cues: Second, hard commission caps.
For individual health insurance, distributors such as brokers and banks can
earn 15% on a first sale, and only 5% on renewals.
Agents get 20% and 10%.
On single-premium savings policies, distributors get 1%.

beats.say: Third, banks. No more making a loan conditional on buying insurance, and no volume linked or reward linked incentives for bank staff selling insurance. IRDAI says mis-selling is more prevalent in banks.
beats.cap: Third, banks. No more making a loan conditional on buying insurance, and no "volume linked or reward linked incentive for bank or NBFC staff selling insurance". IRDAI says mis-selling "is more prevalent in banks".
cues: Third, banks.
No more making a loan conditional on buying insurance,
and no "volume linked or reward linked incentive for bank or NBFC staff
selling insurance".
IRDAI says mis-selling "is more prevalent in banks".

beats.say: Chapter three. Who gives up margin.
beats.cap: Chapter three. Who gives up margin.
cues: Chapter three.
Who gives up margin.

beats.say: High commission insurers first. Last year, private life insurers paid nine percent of premium as commission on average, in a range from three to thirty nine percent. Private general insurers paid over twenty percent. Public sector general insurers paid eleven.
beats.cap: High-commission insurers first. In FY26, private life insurers paid 9% of premium as commission on average, in a range from 3% to 39%. Private general insurers paid "over 20%". Public-sector general insurers paid 11%.
cues: High-commission insurers first.
In FY26, private life insurers paid 9% of premium as commission on average,
in a range from 3% to 39%.
Private general insurers paid "over 20%".
Public-sector general insurers paid 11%.

beats.say: Standalone health insurers, IRDAI says, have largely channelled underwriting margins into commissions and operating expenses rather than lower premiums. A five percent cap on distributors' renewals goes straight at that model.
beats.cap: Standalone health insurers, IRDAI says, "have largely channelled underwriting margins into commissions and operating expenses rather than lower premiums". A 5% cap on distributors' renewals goes straight at that model.
cues: Standalone health insurers, IRDAI says,
"have largely channelled underwriting margins into commissions and operating
expenses rather than lower premiums".
A 5% cap on distributors' renewals goes straight at that model.

beats.say: And banks. They account for nearly sixty eight thousand crore rupees of the sampled life premium sold through corporate agents. Capped commissions, no bundling and no staff incentives all cut the fee income banks earn from insurance. No bank has filed an estimate.
beats.cap: And banks. They account for nearly ₹68,000 crore of the sampled life premium sold through corporate agents. Capped commissions, no bundling and no staff incentives all cut the fee income banks earn from insurance. No bank has filed an estimate.
cues: And banks.
They account for nearly ₹68,000 crore of the sampled life premium sold
through corporate agents.
Capped commissions, no bundling and no staff incentives all cut the fee
income banks earn from insurance.
No bank has filed an estimate.

beats.say: Chapter four. Who keeps the moat.
beats.cap: Chapter four. Who keeps the moat.
cues: Chapter four.
Who keeps the moat.

beats.say: The focus moat is cost advantage. The largest private life insurer paid only four percent commission. The only public sector life insurer paid five percent. These insurers are already inside the proposed limits. For them, the reform is not a cost. It is a constraint on their competitors.
beats.cap: The focus moat is cost advantage. The largest private life insurer paid only 4% commission in FY26. The only public-sector life insurer paid 5%. These insurers are already inside the proposed limits. For them, the reform is not a cost. It is a constraint on their competitors.
cues: The focus moat is cost advantage.
The largest private life insurer paid only 4% commission in FY26.
The only public-sector life insurer paid 5%.
These insurers are already inside the proposed limits.
For them, the reform is not a cost.
It is a constraint on their competitors.

beats.say: What weakens is control over the point of sale. The bank branch, the loan desk and the car dealer earned high commissions, in IRDAI's words, from control over customer access.
beats.cap: What weakens is control over the point of sale. The bank branch, the loan desk and the car dealer earned high commissions, in IRDAI's words, from "control over customer access".
cues: What weakens is control over the point of sale.
The bank branch, the loan desk and the car dealer earned high commissions,
in IRDAI's words, from "control over customer access".

beats.say: One number cuts the other way. Only forty eight percent of life policies are still running at the sixty first month. For policies bought online, it is seventy one percent.
beats.cap: One number cuts the other way. Only 48% of life policies are still running at the 61st month. For policies bought online, it is 71%.
cues: One number cuts the other way.
Only 48% of life policies are still running at the 61st month.
For policies bought online, it is 71%.

beats.say: The bear case. It is a draft, and comments close on the twenty fifth of October. Lower commissions may mean lower sales. The margin may go to policyholders rather than insurers. And banks have other levers.

The margin may go to policyholders rather than insurers.
And banks have other levers.
